posts.why: A sentence everyone has written and nobody believes.

tiktok.hook: This site says trusted by many and shows nothing at all.
tiktok.vo: This site says trusted by many, which is a sentence that has never persuaded anybody, because it is the same sentence a business with no customers would write. Vague trust is not weak trust, it is no trust, and it is doing damage, because it tells the reader you have nothing to show and decided to describe it instead.
tiktok.cap: "Trusted by many" is what a business with nothing to show writes.
tiktok.body: Trusted by many, loved by clients, quality guaranteed — sentences a business with no customers would also write. Vague trust is not weak trust. It is no trust, and it quietly tells the reader you had nothing to show.

instagram.cap: If it would also be true of a business with no customers, delete it.
instagram.body: The test is simple: could a business with zero customers write this sentence? If yes, it is decoration, and the reader knows it before you do.

facebook.body:
A site I read this week says 'trusted by many' and shows nothing at all.

That is the sentence a business with no customers would write.

Vague trust is not weak trust. It is no trust — and it tells the reader you had nothing to show, so you described it instead.

What could you show this week?

posts.why: Removes the excuse that blocks most new businesses.

tiktok.hook: You have no testimonials and you are not stuck. You have process and photographs.
tiktok.vo: You have no testimonials and you are not stuck, because you have process and photographs. Show the fabric being cut, the dough being proved, the paint being mixed, the code being written. Process is proof when results are new, and it is more interesting than a quote from somebody nobody has heard of.
tiktok.cap: Process is proof when results are new. Photograph your hands.
tiktok.body: No clients yet does not mean no proof. Photograph the cutting, the proving, the mixing, the wiring. Process is proof when results are new, and it is more watchable than a quote.

instagram.cap: Show the work being done. That is a testimonial with no words.
instagram.body: A photo of the actual process answers the question a testimonial is trying to answer: is this a real person who can do the thing?

facebook.body:
You have no testimonials and you are not stuck.

You have process and photographs. The fabric being cut. The dough being proved. The paint being mixed. The wiring being finished.

Process is proof when results are new, and it is more convincing than a quote from someone nobody has heard of.

What could you photograph tomorrow?

posts.topic: Show the work, not the praise
posts.why: A structural alternative to the testimonial section.

tiktok.hook: A before and after beats a quote. Show the work, not the praise.
tiktok.vo: A before and after beats a quote, because a quote is a claim about you and a before and after is evidence. Same angle, same light, same corner of the room, and no adjectives anywhere. If you have not got a before photo, take one on the next job, before you touch anything, and you will have a year of proof by December.
tiktok.cap: Same angle, same light, no adjectives. That is a case study.
tiktok.body: A before and after is evidence. A quote is a claim. Take the before photo on your next job, before you touch anything, and you will have a year of proof by December.

instagram.cap: Start photographing the before. Most people only photograph the after.
instagram.body: The before photo is the one everybody forgets, and it is the one that makes the after mean anything.

facebook.body:
A before and after beats a quote.

A quote is a claim about you. A before and after is evidence, and it needs no adjectives at all — same angle, same light, same corner of the room.

If you have never taken a before photo, take one on the next job, before you touch anything.

By December you will have a year of proof.

posts.why: Turns a limitation into a positioning strategy.

tiktok.hook: Your honesty is currently your only proof. Use it instead of inventing one.
beats: But you can say what you will not do
tiktok.vo: Your honesty is currently your only proof, and it is a better one than you think. You can say what the pack will not do, what the price does not include, how long it will actually take, and who should not buy it. All four are checkable, and all four are rarer than a testimonial.
tiktok.cap: Saying what it will not do is proof. It is also rare, which makes it valuable.
tiktok.body: When you have no results, sell the things that are checkable: what it costs, what is not included, how long it takes, who should not buy it. Rarer than a testimonial, and harder to fake.

instagram.body: Every limit you state is a small demonstration that you are not hiding anything, and customers read limits as competence even when they do not buy.

facebook.body:
When you have no results yet, your honesty is your only proof — and it is better than you think.

You can say what it will not do. What the price does not include. How long it will actually take. Who should not buy it.

All four are checkable. All four are rarer than a testimonial.

Which one are you hiding?

posts.topic: A real chat beat a page of claims
posts.why: Permission and anonymising are part of the lesson.

tiktok.hook: A screenshot of one real chat outsold a whole page of claims.
beats: The chat said it is ₦8,000 and I can deliver Thursday
tiktok.vo: A screenshot of one real chat, with permission and the name blurred, did more than a whole page of claims about quality and service. Because the chat showed the actual thing: a price, a date, and a person answering. That is the proof a new business has sitting in its phone already, and almost nobody uses it because it does not feel like marketing.
tiktok.cap: One real chat, permission asked, name blurred. Better than a page of claims.
tiktok.body: The page said quality and service. The chat said eight thousand naira and Thursday. One of those is evidence and the other is decoration, and the evidence was already in the phone.

instagram.cap: The proof you need is already in your chat history.
instagram.body: Ask before you post, blur anything identifying, and use the message that shows a real price and a real answer. That is the honest version of a testimonial.

facebook.body:
A screenshot of one real chat did more than a whole page of claims about quality and service.

Because the chat showed the actual thing: a price, a date, and a person answering.

Two rules: ask permission, and blur the name.

That proof is already sitting in your phone. Almost nobody uses it, because it does not feel like marketing.

Would you show one?

posts.why: A tiny assignment with a deadline.

tiktok.hook: Take three photos of your process this week. Not the finished thing. The middle.
tiktok.vo: Take three photos of your process this week, and not the finished thing. The middle: the cutting, the waiting, the fixing, the thing going wrong and being put right. Nobody photographs the middle, which is why the middle is the most interesting thing you own, and it is free to make.
tiktok.cap: Three photos of the middle. Everyone photographs the finish.
tiktok.body: The cutting, the waiting, the fixing, the bit that went wrong. Nobody photographs the middle, which is exactly why the middle is the most interesting asset you have.

instagram.cap: The middle is where trust is built and where nobody is looking.
instagram.body: A finished product looks like every other finished product. The middle looks like you, and that is the part people remember.

facebook.body:
Take three photos of your process this week. Not the finished thing — the middle.

The cutting. The waiting. The fixing. The bit that went wrong and was put right.

Nobody photographs the middle, which is exactly why it is the most interesting thing your business owns.

It is also free.

What would your three be?

posts.topic: A case study with no numbers
posts.why: Frees people from waiting for impressive data.

tiktok.hook: A case study with no numbers is still a case study.
tiktok.vo: A case study with no numbers is still a case study, because the reader is not looking for a percentage, they are looking for a shape: what was the problem, what did you do, and what is different now. Three sentences, in words, about a real job. Percentages are nice and almost nobody has them in month one.
tiktok.cap: Problem, action, what changed. No percentages needed.
tiktok.body: Three sentences about a real job: what was wrong, what you did, what is different now. The reader is looking for a shape, not a statistic.

instagram.cap: A percentage is nice. A story is possible today.
instagram.body: You can write this tonight about any finished job, even a small one, even the first one. Three sentences and a photo.

facebook.body:
A case study with no numbers is still a case study.

What was the problem? What did you do? What is different now?

Three sentences, in words, about a real job. That is it.

Readers are looking for a shape, not a percentage. Percentages are nice and almost nobody has them in month one.

Which job would you write up?

posts.why: Witnesses rank our own thesis above the obvious answer.

tiktok.hook: I asked what would make people trust a new business. Seeing the work beat reviews.
tiktok.vo: I asked what would make people trust a business they had never used. Seeing the work came first, ahead of reviews, ahead of follower counts. Not the finished photo, the making of it, because a finished photo can be borrowed and a process cannot. That is the cheapest trust in Lagos and nobody is selling it.
tiktok.cap: "Show me the work" beat reviews. Not the star rating. The work.
tiktok.body: Seeing the work came ahead of reviews and follower counts. A finished photo can be borrowed from anywhere; a process is harder to fake and much more persuasive.

instagram.cap: Trust is cheaper to build with a camera than with a testimonial.
instagram.body: Most new businesses wait to be trusted. The fastest route is to show the work being done, this week, with no numbers attached.

facebook.body:
I asked what would make people trust a business they had never used.

'Seeing the work' came first — ahead of reviews, well ahead of follower counts.

Not the finished photo. The making of it. A finished photo can be borrowed. A process is harder to fake.

It is the cheapest trust in Lagos and almost nobody is selling it.

What could you show?

posts.topic: We have no client results to show yet
posts.why: The most disarming possible advertisement for ourselves.

tiktok.hook: We do not have a wall of client results to show you yet. Here is what we do instead.
tiktok.vo: We do not have a wall of client results to show yet, so I am not going to pretend otherwise. What we do instead is publish the method, in public, every day, with the limits attached. If the method is any good you can judge it without our numbers, and if it is not you will know by Friday, which is fairer than a logo.
tiktok.cap: No results wall. The method, published daily, with limits. Packs from ₦5,000. WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.
tiktok.body: We do not have a wall of client results yet, so we are not going to fake one. What we publish instead is the method, daily, with the limits attached. Judge the method, not our logos.

instagram.cap: Judge the method. It is more checkable than a logo.
instagram.body: Anyone can borrow a logo. The method is either useful by Friday or it is not, and you can test that without taking our word for anything.

facebook.body:
We do not have a wall of client results to show you yet, so I will not pretend otherwise.

What we publish instead is the method, daily, in public, with the limits attached.

If the method is any good you can judge it without our numbers. If it is not, you will know by Friday — which is fairer than a logo.

Packs from ₦5,000. Message PACK on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

posts.why: Naming the request makes the refusal credible.

tiktok.hook: Someone asked us to write a testimonial for them to publish. We said no.
beats: And they would have to defend it
tiktok.vo: Someone asked us to write a customer testimonial that they could publish as if a customer had said it. We said no. Not for moral reasons only, though those are enough, but because they would have to defend that sentence for as long as the business exists, to anyone who asked a follow-up question. Ten minutes of writing, years of maintenance.
tiktok.cap: A fake testimonial is ten minutes of writing and years of defending it.
tiktok.body: They wanted a testimonial written by us and published as a customer's words. Ten minutes of writing, then years of defending a sentence to anyone who asks a follow-up question.

slides: You would have to defend it forever
instagram.cap: A lie in the mouth of a customer is a debt you never finish paying.
instagram.body: The problem is not getting caught. The problem is that you would have to remember the lie and be consistent about it for the life of the business.

facebook.body:
Someone asked us to write a customer testimonial that they could publish as if a customer had said it.

We said no.

Not only for moral reasons, though those are enough — but because they would have to defend that sentence for as long as the business exists, to anyone who asks a follow-up question.

Ten minutes of writing. Years of maintenance.

Have you ever spotted a fake one?

posts.topic: Ask permission to show one chat
posts.why: Turns the audience into suppliers of tomorrow's proof.

tiktok.hook: Ask three customers if you can screenshot one chat. Then blur the name.
beats: Thank them by doing it well
tiktok.vo: Ask three customers whether you can screenshot one message and post it, and say exactly what it is for. Then blur the name and anything else that identifies them. Most will say yes, because being shown as a real customer is a small compliment, and the ones who say no will respect you for asking instead of doing it.
tiktok.cap: Ask plainly. Blur everything. Most people say yes.
tiktok.body: Ask three customers if you can screenshot one message, say exactly what it is for, and blur anything that identifies them. Most say yes, and the ones who say no respect you for asking.

instagram.cap: Permission is the whole difference between proof and a problem.
instagram.body: A real message with the name blurred is proof. The same message posted without asking is a risk you did not need to take.

facebook.body:
Ask three customers whether you can screenshot one message and post it.

Ask plainly. Say exactly what it is for. Then blur the name and anything else that identifies them.

Most will say yes — being shown as a real customer is a small compliment. The ones who say no will respect you for asking instead of just doing it.

Who would you ask?
